title: Coin Flip & Dice Roller Online
description: Flip up to 100 coins or roll up to 10 dice (d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20) with secure randomness, totals, heads and tails counts, and a history of results.
quickAnswer: Choose Coin or Dice, set how many, and press Flip or Roll. Each coin has exactly a 50% chance of heads, and each face of a die is equally likely, because results come from your browser's secure random generator with rejection sampling. Dice show every face and the total, and the last 20 results stay in the history.

formula.title: Probabilities
formula.expression: P(heads) = 1/2   ·   P(any face of a dN) = 1/N   ·   Sum of k dice ranges from k to k × N
formula.explanation: Every flip and roll is independent: earlier results do not change the next one. For one die all faces are equally likely, but sums of several dice are not: with 2d6 there are 36 equally likely combinations, six of which add up to 7, so 7 is the most common total (1 in 6) and 2 or 12 the rarest (1 in 36). The average total of k dice with N sides is k × (N + 1) ÷ 2.

commonMistakes.title: The gambler's fallacy
commonMistakes.description: After five heads in a row, tails is still exactly 50%. Coins and dice have no memory, so past results never make a particular outcome "due".

commonMistakes.title: Assuming all dice totals are equally likely
commonMistakes.description: With two dice, 7 comes up six times as often as 2 or 12. Only single-die results are evenly spread.

commonMistakes.title: Expecting exactly 50 heads in 100 flips
commonMistakes.description: Exactly 50 heads happens only about 8% of the time. Results between 40 and 60 are normal; it takes many thousands of flips for the proportion to settle close to 50%.

commonMistakes.title: Using a predictable random source
commonMistakes.description: Simple generators such as Math.random() are fine for animations but not for anything where fairness matters. This tool uses crypto.getRandomValues with rejection sampling so no face is favoured.

faqs.q: Is the online coin flip fair?
faqs.a: Yes. Each flip uses your browser's cryptographically secure random generator, so heads and tails each have exactly a 50% chance, and no flip depends on the previous one.
Choose Dice, set the number of dice to 2 and the type to d6, then press Roll. You will see both dice and their total, which can be from 2 to 12.

faqs.q: What is the most common total with two dice?
faqs.a: 7. Six of the 36 combinations add up to 7 (1+6, 2+5, 3+4, 4+3, 5+2, 6+1), so it comes up 1 time in 6 on average.
d4, d6, d8, d10, d12 and d20, up to 10 dice at once, the standard set used in tabletop role-playing games.

faqs.q: How many coins can I flip at once?
faqs.a: Up to 100. The result shows every coin and counts the heads and tails.

faqs.q: Can I see my previous results?
faqs.a: Yes. The history keeps your last 20 flips and rolls on this page. It is cleared when you leave or press Clear history.

faqs.q: Can I turn off the animation?
faqs.a: The flip and roll animation is skipped automatically if your device is set to reduce motion.

dice-odds-at-a-glance.heading: Dice Odds at a Glance
dice-odds-at-a-glance.p1: One die gives every face the same chance. Add more dice and the totals bunch up in the middle, which is why 7 is the number to watch in board games played with two six-sided dice.
dice-odds-at-a-glance.caption1: Ranges, averages and single-face chances for common dice

when-to-flip-a-coin-or.heading: When to Flip a Coin or Roll a Die Online
when-to-flip-a-coin-or.li1: Settling a decision: a coin flip is the classic fair tie-breaker between two options.
when-to-flip-a-coin-or.li2: Board games and role-playing games: replace missing dice, or roll handfuls of d6 or a d20 quickly with the total worked out.
when-to-flip-a-coin-or.li3: Teaching probability: flip 100 coins several times to show how the heads count varies, or compare 2d6 totals with the odds table above.
when-to-flip-a-coin-or.li4: Random choices: for a choice among more than six options, use the random number generator or the random name picker.
when-to-flip-a-coin-or.p1: Physical coins and dice can be slightly biased by their shape and how they are thrown. A secure software generator does not have that problem: every outcome is exactly equally likely. Results are generated in your browser and the history stays on this page only.
